Aiṣā-vīra.--The Śatapatha brāhmaṇa once refers to the aiṣā-vīras as officiating at a sacrifice, with the implication that they were bad sacrificers. Sāyaṇa regards the word as a proper name (‘descendants of Eṣavīra’), denoting the members of a despised family. But Roth may be right in explaining the word both in the passage mentioned above and elsewhere as meaning ‘weak’ or ‘insignificant man.’
Foot notes xi. 2, 7, 32.
In the St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
In Bo7htlingk's Dictionary, s.v. (‘one who wishes to be a man, but is not’). Cf. Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, ix. 5, 1, 16; kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa, i. 1, where, however, Lindner's edition reads saiṣā vīra iva. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 228; Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 44, 45.
